name: aomega-m3-pretzel-symmetry-adapted-basis
description: The Z/2 symmetry X <-> 1/X of the pretzel's residue families, the symmetry-adapted basis that lifts Part 15's rank 4 to 6, and its (4,1,1) grading matching GZ's printed weight decomposition.
verdict: DERIVED: X <-> 1/X is an exact Z/2 on the six residue families — it exchanges the two unit families and fixes each parity class — so Part 15's degeneracy is the symmetry, not an accident: the antisymmetric part must vanish at the fixed point. Dividing by the antisymmetric coordinate W = X - 1/X lifts the rank 4 -> 5, and the one residual coincidence (sym(F1,F2) = F3(0,0) at X = 1) vanishes to order exactly 2, so dividing it by W^2 completes the basis to RANK 6. The resulting grading by order of vanishing is (4, 1, 1) — exactly GZ's printed weight decomposition for this knot, derived here from the residues rather than transcribed. So the meridian deformation does carry GZ's eps-expansion, not as an evaluation of the separated families (Part 15's negative stands) but in the orders of vanishing of their symmetry-adapted combinations. The Z/2 is the same one the operator route reaches independently (#7333). T1, transporting GZ Obs 3.9 to this basis: {'zeta=x': False, 'zeta=x^{1/2}': False, 'zeta=1/x': False}.
